publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Corporation Division
ownership: Official active business-registration public records published through Oregon's Open Data Portal
program_use_authorization: Oregon's Open Data Program defines open data as data that can be freely used, modified, and shared by anyone for any purpose and is available at no direct cost.
source_access: Public anonymous read-only HTTPS Socrata API.
allowed_use: official HTTPS metadata and selected-field API queries
redistribution of approved normalized public fields with source attribution and semantic limitations
prohibited_use: representing Active as independent proof of current operations, legality, solvency, public access, licensure, or an open storefront
representing a principal place of business as a verified current physical operating site
representing an assumed business name as a legal organization or inferring its owner
representing this state registry as every business operating in Oregon or the United States
exporting associated-person names, registered-agent fields, authorized-representative fields, or mailing-address rows
merging registrations across sources without versioned evidence
attribution: Source: Oregon Secretary of State, Corporation Division, Active Businesses - ALL, via Oregon's Open Data Portal.
retention: Indefinite for immutable selected-field source and approved normalized records unless an approved retention rule applies.
redistribution: Approved normalized fields may be redistributed under the Oregon Open Data Program use authorization with source attribution, source refresh timestamp, source checksum, provenance, field exclusions, and status/address limitations retained; the selected-field source snapshot remains internal.
personal_data_handling: Business names and principal-place addresses are public registration fields but can identify a sole proprietor or home address. The connector excludes every first, middle, last, and suffix field; entity-of-record names and numbers; all registered-agent and authorized-representative rows; and mailing-address rows. Downstream use must retain the public-record and non-site warning.
